messages:
Will: Morning team, day 1! Quick privacy question before I enroll my personal Mac: does MDM allow admins to see my files, browsing history, or screenshots? Also, will enrollment change FileVault or my Apple ID? When's the phishing sim + security training due?

Aisha: Welcome Will \u2705 Short answer: MDM reports compliance metadata (OS version, device model, encryption status, passcode enabled) and the device hostname. It does NOT upload personal files, browsing history, or app contents by default. Enrollment does not change your Apple ID or disable FileVault. Training: https://learning.redwood/security-foundations  due within 7 days. Phish sim scheduled: 2026-04-14 11:00 PT.

Will: OK thanks. If I run into an enrollment error, what logs would support troubleshooting and how can I share without exposing personal stuff?

Aisha: Usually we ask for system logs or a sysdiagnose bundle on macOS. You can inspect and redact before sharing. For mac: run `sudo sysdiagnose -f ~/Desktop/` then compress and DM via our secure upload link. If you're uncomfortable, request a loaner corp laptop instead. Docs: https://intranet.redwood/it/support-privacy

IT-ops: FYI if you prefer not to enroll personal devices we can overnight a loaner. Submit the hardware request form and mark "privacy exception" and we'll prioritize. Typical delivery 24-48h.

secops-bot: Reminder: New hires must complete "Security Foundations" training within 7 days. Next phishing simulation: 2026-04-14 11:00 PT.

Claire: Enrollment steps (mac): 1) Install Company Portal 2) Sign in with SSO 3) Approve the management profile in System Preferences > Profiles 4) Verify FileVault: `fdesetup status` should return "FileVault is On." If you see Activation Lock or DEP/ABM prompts, stop and DM me.

Will: One more: does enrolling force all traffic through company VPN/proxy? I sometimes need local resources.

Aisha: Good question  split tunneling is enabled for user devices by default, so not all traffic is routed through corporate proxy. Only traffic to protected hosts/services is routed. Enterprise-enrolled devices (corp-owned) may have tighter rules.

Will: Great, I'll enroll tonight and paste the `fdesetup` output if anything looks odd. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
